title: Transfer audit for 2026
prompt: The auditors review every transfer requested in 2026. Write `solve(transfers)` so it returns `transfer_id`, `status`, `reference` and `check` for those transfers.
rules: Keep transfers whose `requested_at` is on or after 1 January 2026 00:00:00.

`check` is the first problem found, in this order: `missing account` (either account missing), `same account`, `bad amount` (missing or not more than 0), `bad reversal` (`reversal_of` is set but `status` isn't exactly `completed`). Otherwise it's `ok`.
A missing `reference` shows as `(none)`. Return the four columns, in that order, keeping duplicates.
hints: Filter first with `F.col("requested_at") >= "2026-01-01"`. A transfer with no time isn't on or after anything, so it drops out.
In the reversal rule, a missing status isn't `completed`, but `status != "completed"` is NULL for it. Add `F.col("status").isNull() |`.
`F.coalesce(F.col("reference"), F.lit("(none)"))` or `na.fill` fills the missing references.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(transfers):
    # Return transfer_id, status, reference and check for transfers requested in 2026.
    return transfers
explanation: Three earlier lessons meet here. A filter keeps 2026: `F.col("requested_at") >= "2026-01-01"`. A `when` chain gives the first problem: `F.when(F.col("from_account_id").isNull() | F.col("to_account_id").isNull(), "missing account").when(F.col("from_account_id") == F.col("to_account_id"), "same account").when(F.col("amount").isNull() | (F.col("amount") <= 0), "bad amount").when(F.col("reversal_of").isNotNull() & (F.col("status").isNull() | (F.col("status") != "completed")), "bad reversal").otherwise("ok")`. The missing-account rule comes first so the same-account test only meets two real ids. In the reversal rule, a missing status would make `!= "completed"` NULL and the transfer would pass as `ok`, so it's caught with `isNull()`. Finally `F.coalesce(F.col("reference"), F.lit("(none)"))` fills the reference; `transfers.na.fill("(none)", subset=["reference"])` before the `select` works too.
